userStories.title: Catalog tiers for agent spend and account writes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Raise the five named catalog risks while preserving all other permissions and the catalog's existing approval derivation.

**Motivation** — `classifyRisk` in `apps/api/src/permissions/catalog.ts` returns `medium` for any key that matches no rule, and `medium` gives the approval default `none`.

**Approach** — `classifyRisk(key)` in `apps/api/src/permissions/catalog.ts`.
- Target: additionally `fleet.thread.preapprove` is `critical`, and the members of a new exported `SPEND_AND_ACCOUNT_WRITE_KEYS: ReadonlySet<string>` (`fleet.job.dispatch`, `fleet.job.config.edit`, `fleet.schedule.create`, `user.update`) are `high`. `buildEntry` is unchanged.
Tiers follow the owner's 2026-11-14 rulings. Other spend-adjacent keys keep their tier (see Out of Scope).
Making the key user-only is not possible: `RoleAdminService.assertPrincipalType` would then refuse binding the Developer role to any agent. Risk `critical` gives the key the `human` approval floor instead.

Update `apps/api/src/permissions/catalog.spec.ts`: the test's own `expectedRisk(key)` mirror of `classifyRisk`, checked against every catalog key, must return `critical` for `fleet.thread.preapprove` and `high` for `fleet.job.dispatch`, `fleet.job.config.edit`, `fleet.schedule.create` and `user.update`; every other key's expected risk stays. High keys retain their existing floor and default to agent approval; thread preapproval retains both principal types. Direct humans remain governed by the existing gate branch that satisfies every mode.

**Scope** — In: catalog set/classification, its independent unit mirror and unchanged undefined results for unknown-key lookups. Out: route regression updates belong to US-002; the preapproval controller remains unchanged.
- Retiering `fleet.schedule.update`, `fleet.schedule.enable`, `fleet.job.requeue` or any key other than the five named in this spec; they keep their current risk.

**Interface** — `SPEND_AND_ACCOUNT_WRITE_KEYS: ReadonlySet<string>`; `classifyRisk(key)`; `findCatalogEntry(key: string): PermissionCatalogEntry | undefined`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] findCatalogEntry('fleet.job.dispatch') returns risk: 'high' and approval.default: 'agent'.
AC-2 [unit] findCatalogEntry('fleet.job.config.edit') returns risk: 'high' and approval.default: 'agent'.
AC-3 [unit] findCatalogEntry('fleet.schedule.create') returns risk: 'high' and approval.default: 'agent'.
AC-4 [unit] findCatalogEntry('user.update') returns risk: 'high' and approval.default: 'agent'.
AC-5 [unit] findCatalogEntry('fleet.thread.preapprove') returns risk: 'critical' and approval.floor: 'human'.
AC-6 [unit] findCatalogEntry('fleet.thread.preapprove').principals equals ['user', 'agent'].
AC-7 [unit] SPEND_AND_ACCOUNT_WRITE_KEYS is importable from permissions/catalog.ts with exactly the members fleet.job.dispatch, fleet.job.config.edit, fleet.schedule.create and user.update.
AC-8 [unit] findCatalogEntry('fleet.schedule.update').risk and findCatalogEntry('fleet.job.requeue').risk are both 'medium'.
AC-9 [unit, negative regression] findCatalogEntry('fleet.job.not-a-permission') returns undefined rather than synthesizing an entry for an unknown permission key.

userStories.title: Routes honour the new approval tiers
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make the existing route and MCP contracts honor the new no-policy agent approval defaults without changing immediate direct-human execution.

**Motivation** — An agent with global Admin can disable other admins with no approval.

**Approach** — `apps/api/src/approvals/approval-gate.service.ts`: a direct human satisfies every mode; only non-human callers open an approval request.
`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.controller.ts`: `POST projects/:slug/fleet/jobs` is `@ApprovalGated()` and runs through `ApprovalRouteGate`, which returns `202` with the pending request.
An authorized agent holding the route's required permission key (and project reach where applicable), calling the dispatch, schedule-create or admin user PATCH route with no approval policy now gets `202` and a pending request; an authorized human still runs at once. A caller missing the required key still receives `403` without an approval request; approval does not substitute for permission. The existing agent-dispatch and agent-schedule tests move to the new expectation.

Preserve the specified regressions individually: in `enforce-fleet-jobs.integration.spec.ts`, AC-4 now expects `202` with a pending `fleet.job.dispatch` request and no job row; AC-5 and AC-6 keep their stored-actor and activity assertions by seeding a `none` approval policy for the agent in their setup. In `enforce-fleet-schedules.integration.spec.ts`, AC-5 now expects `202` with a pending `fleet.schedule.create` request, and AC-6 keeps its stored-creator assertion by seeding a `none` approval policy for the agent. In `gated-fleet-job-routes.integration.spec.ts`, existing AC-15 changes from immediate/no request to `202`, exactly one pending `fleet.job.dispatch` request and no job row for feature `ac-15`. In `permissions-assistant-tools.integration.spec.ts`, existing AC-6 seeds a `none` policy for `fleet.job.dispatch` for that agent in p1 and retains its QUEUED-job/requested-by-agent assertions through `koda_dispatch_job`. In `gated-admin-write-routes.integration.spec.ts`, add the no-policy agent user PATCH case; existing explicit-wait-policy cases stay. Use isolated policy fixtures so no-policy cases genuinely have no override. The catalog change should activate existing gate wiring; repair production wiring only if the route fails to honor that established contract, not by introducing a parallel gate.

**Scope** — In: route behavior and real HTTP/Postgres regression updates explicitly assigned to this binding story. Out: catalog risk definitions belong to US-001; project reach optimization and runner identity belong to US-006 and US-008.

**Interface** — `POST /api/projects/:slug/fleet/jobs`; `POST /api/projects/:slug/fleet/schedules`; `PATCH /api/admin/users/:id`; `koda_dispatch_job`. Existing pending approval envelopes and permissionKey identifiers are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] An agent holding fleet.job.dispatch in the project, with no approval policy seeded, calling POST /api/projects/:slug/fleet/jobs with a valid RUN body gets 202 with a pending request whose permissionKey is fleet.job.dispatch.
AC-2 [integration] After that 202, no FleetJob row exists for the request.
AC-3 [integration] A user holding fleet.job.dispatch, with no approval policy seeded, calling the same route with the same body gets 201.

AC-4 [integration] An agent holding fleet.schedule.create in the project, with no approval policy seeded, calling POST /api/projects/:slug/fleet/schedules with a valid body gets 202 with a pending fleet.schedule.create request.

AC-5 [integration] An agent holding user.update globally, with no approval policy seeded, calling PATCH /api/admin/users/:id with { "disabled": true } gets 202 with a pending user.update request, and the target user's disabled stays false.

AC-6 [integration, negative regression] When an authenticated project-member agent lacks fleet.job.dispatch, POST /api/projects/:slug/fleet/jobs with a valid RUN body returns 403 without opening an approval request.

routing.reasoning: Existing ApprovalRouteGate wiring already supplies the behavior; scoped policy fixtures and HTTP/MCP expectation updates are standard changes, while permission enforcement requires the security override.

userStories.title: Stop a failed flow with internal_error
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a locked, audited internal-error stop primitive for live and waiting-merge flows.

**Motivation** — A flow that hits an undeclared error never changes state, so `listAdvanceable` returns it again every `flowTickMs` (30 s).

**Approach** — `FlowStopReason` in `apps/api/src/fleet/flows/flow-step-decision.ts` gains `'internal_error'`.
`awaitedFeatures(flow)` in `apps/api/src/fleet/flows/fleet-flow-feature-passes.ts`.
- Target: exported, unchanged otherwise. The same file gains an exported pure function `failureStopFeature(flow: FleetFlowRecord): FleetFlowFeatureRecord`: for a WAITING_MERGE flow the first awaited feature, otherwise the active feature, and in both cases the first feature by position when there is none.
`FleetFlowAdvanceService` gains `stopFailedFlow(flowId: string, detail: string, now: Date): Promise<boolean>`. It reads the flow; for APPROVED or RUNNING it writes the stop through `writeStop`, for WAITING_MERGE it takes `lockWaitingMerge` and writes the stop through `writeDecision`, in both cases with reason `internal_error` and the feature `failureStopFeature` picks. It returns `true` when a stop was written and `false` when the flow is gone or in any other state. An empty `detail` is stored as `internal error`.

Reuse the existing parent/flow lock ordering and approval-generation checks, and ensure the boolean reflects a real write even if the flow changes state between the read and lock. `writeDecision` bounds `detail` to `FLOW_STOP_DETAIL_MAX` and records the `flow.stopped` activity; retain its audit and stopped outbox behavior rather than writing the row directly. Exercise `failureStopFeature` through this new public method, including WAITING_MERGE, and expose `awaitedFeatures` without changing its selection rule. Add `apps/api/test/integration/fleet/fleet-flow-failure-stop.integration.spec.ts` using the existing advance integration fixture pattern; pure selectors can be covered in an existing adjacent unit spec.

**Scope** — In: reason union, exported selection helpers, public stop primitive and transactional persistence behavior. Out: retry counting/cursor belongs to US-004 and watch throttling to US-005.
- Web i18n labels for the `internal_error` stop reason; the web flow page and notifications fall back to `humanizeCode`, which renders "Internal error".
- Splitting `fleet-flow-advance.service.ts` (1008 lines) below the 800-line limit; new flow-stop selection logic goes into `fleet-flow-feature-passes.ts` instead of growing the service further.

**Interface** — `failureStopFeature(flow: FleetFlowRecord): FleetFlowFeatureRecord`; `stopFailedFlow(flowId: string, detail: string, now: Date): Promise<boolean>`; exported `awaitedFeatures(flow)`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] stopFailedFlow(flowId, 'boom', now) on a RUNNING flow returns true.
AC-2 [integration] After that call the flow row has state STOPPED, stopReason internal_error and stopDetail boom.
AC-3 [integration] After that call a flow.stopped activity row exists for the flow.
AC-4 [integration] stopFailedFlow on a WAITING_MERGE flow returns true and leaves the row with state STOPPED and stopReason internal_error.
AC-5 [integration] stopFailedFlow on a flow already in state STOPPED returns false and leaves its stopReason and endedAt unchanged.
AC-6 [unit] failureStopFeature on a WAITING_MERGE flow whose features are MERGED at position 0 and awaiting at position 1 returns the position-1 feature.
AC-7 [unit] failureStopFeature on a RUNNING flow with no active feature returns the feature at the lowest position.
AC-8 [integration] stopFailedFlow(flowId, '', now) on a RUNNING flow stores stopDetail internal error.
AC-9 [unit] awaitedFeatures is importable from fleet-flow-feature-passes.ts and returns the awaiting features of a flow in position order.
AC-10 [integration, failure handling] When the flow is gone or has left APPROVED, RUNNING and WAITING_MERGE before the stop, stopFailedFlow returns false and writes nothing.

routing.reasoning: The new public method and pure selector reuse existing lockLive, lockWaitingMerge and writeDecision paths; no new transaction abstraction or integration is needed, so ordinary TDD with real-DB stop tests is sufficient.

userStories.title: Bound flow failures and resume ticker pagination fairly
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Stop repeatedly failing flows after five consecutive errors and carry fair pagination across bounded ticks.

**Motivation** — Each tick starts from the lowest flow id and stops at 500 flows, so flows beyond 500 are never reached while lower ids stay advanceable.

**Approach** — `FleetFlowTicker.tick(now)` in `apps/api/src/fleet/flows/fleet-flow.ticker.ts`.
- Target: the first `listAdvanceable` call of a tick uses the cursor the previous tick left: the last listed id after a tick that hit the page limit, `null` after a tick that reached a short page. A `listAdvanceable` that throws leaves the cursor unchanged. The ticker counts consecutive advance failures per flow id; a resolved advance deletes the count. When a count reaches the exported `FLOW_FAILURE_STOP_AFTER` (`5`), the ticker calls `engine.stopFailedFlow(flowId, <that error's message>, now)` inside the same `runAsSystem('flow', ..., { onBehalfOf: <flow creator> })` it uses for `advance`, and deletes the count when the call resolves. A rejected `stopFailedFlow` is logged and the count kept.

The flow failure counts, the ticker cursor and the merge-watch timestamps live in process memory. The API is single-replica by ruling, so no column or migration is added. A restart resets them.
- failure counts: after a tick that started at `afterId` `null` and reached a short page (so it listed every advanceable flow), the ticker deletes the count of every flow id that tick did not list. A tick that resumed from a cursor prunes nothing, because it never saw the lower ids;
- the cursor is a single value.

Retain PAGE_SIZE 50, MAX_PAGES 10, the existing interval entry point and poll single-flight behavior. Commit a cursor update only after successful listing for the entire tick; a failure on any page preserves the cursor left before this tick. Fewer than five consecutive failures are logged and retried next tick; a resolved stop, including false, clears the count. A rejected stop cannot reject the tick or prevent later flows advancing; retry stopping on the next failure. Every stop must execute in the same system writer/onBehalfOf attribution as the advance, not outside that context. Extend the ticker's mocked engine with stopFailedFlow and use multi-tick tests on one ticker instance; capture context inside the stub and assert outside the catchable callback.

**Scope** — In: ticker cursor, consecutive-failure bookkeeping, explicit pruning and consuming US-003's stop seam. Out: public stop implementation is US-003; merge-watch timestamp/config logic is US-005.
- A database column or migration for the flow failure counts, the ticker cursor or the merge-watch timestamps; they are in-memory because the API is single-replica by ruling.

**Interface** — exported `FLOW_FAILURE_STOP_AFTER` (`5`); `FleetFlowTicker.tick(now)`; `listAdvanceable(limit: number, afterId: string | null): Promise<AdvanceableFlow[]>`; `stopFailedFlow(flowId: string, detail: string, now: Date): Promise<boolean>`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] FLOW_FAILURE_STOP_AFTER is importable from fleet-flow.ticker.ts and equals 5.
AC-2 [unit] With engine.advance rejecting for flow F on 4 consecutive tick calls, engine.stopFailedFlow is never called.
AC-3 [unit] With engine.advance rejecting for flow F with message boom-5 on the 5th consecutive tick, engine.stopFailedFlow is called once with ('F', 'boom-5', now).
AC-4 [unit] Inside that stopFailedFlow call, currentContext() reports the system writer flow acting on behalf of the flow's creator.
AC-5 [unit] Four rejecting ticks for F, one resolving tick, then four rejecting ticks call engine.stopFailedFlow zero times.
AC-6 [unit] After engine.stopFailedFlow resolves for F, one more rejecting tick for F does not call stopFailedFlow.
AC-7 [unit] When engine.stopFailedFlow rejects for F, tick resolves and still advances the next listed flow G in that tick.
AC-8 [unit] After a rejected stopFailedFlow for F, the next rejecting tick for F calls stopFailedFlow again.
AC-9 [unit] Five rejecting ticks for F interleaved with resolving advances for G call stopFailedFlow for F only.

AC-10 [unit] A flow F with 4 recorded failures that a tick starting at afterId null and ending on a short page does not list, then listed and rejecting again, needs 5 more rejecting ticks before stopFailedFlow is called.
AC-14 [unit] A flow F with 4 recorded failures that a tick resumed from a non-null cursor does not list keeps its count: the next rejecting tick for F calls stopFailedFlow.
AC-11 [unit] After a tick whose listAdvanceable calls returned 10 full pages, the next tick's first listAdvanceable call has afterId equal to the id of the last flow of the 10th page.
AC-12 [unit] After a tick whose listAdvanceable returned a short page, the next tick's first listAdvanceable call has afterId null.
AC-13 [unit] After a tick in which listAdvanceable threw, the next tick's first listAdvanceable call has the same afterId as the tick that threw.
AC-15 [unit, failure handling] When listAdvanceable throws, tick rejects with that error, preserving the previously committed cursor.

routing.reasoning: Changes are confined to one existing ticker and its injected unit harness: a counter map, a cursor and existing system-context calls; deterministic multi-tick TDD covers the specified state sequences without a new abstraction.

userStories.title: Throttle completed flow merge watches
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Limit successful per-flow merge watches to the configured interval without hiding errors from the failure budget.

**Motivation** — Each `WAITING_MERGE` flow polls every awaited PR on GitHub every tick.

**Approach** — `IFleetConfig` gains `flowMergePollMs: number`, read from `FLEET_FLOW_MERGE_POLL_MS` (default `120_000`), with the same validation as `FLEET_FLOW_TICK_MS`: an integer from `1_000` to `3_600_000` in the Joi schema (`env.validation.ts`) and an optional string in the env DTO (`fleet.config.ts`). The advance service's `FLEET_CFG` pick gains `'flowMergePollMs'`.
`FleetFlowAdvanceService.advance(flowId, now)`.
- Target: it skips `runMergeWatch` when a timestamp recorded for the flow is less than `flowMergePollMs` before `now`. The timestamp is recorded (as `now`) only when `runMergeWatch` resolves with `kind: 'watched'`.
A merge watch records its timestamp only when `runMergeWatch` resolves with outcome `kind: 'watched'`. A watch that throws, or resolves `retry` (a transient forge or token failure) or `idle`, records nothing, so the next tick runs it again; a throwing watch therefore still reaches the 5-failure stop. A skipped watch resolves `advance` normally and resets the count, which is correct because a skip only follows a completed watch.
- merge-watch timestamps: each time a timestamp is recorded, entries older than `flowMergePollMs` are deleted (an expired entry means the same as no entry);
The flow failure counts, the ticker cursor and the merge-watch timestamps live in process memory. The API is single-replica by ruling, so no column or migration is added. A restart resets them.

Add `apps/api/src/fleet/flows/fleet-flow-merge-poll.spec.ts`, driving the real advance service with the existing merge-watch harness as precedent. Add `flowMergePollMs: 0` to `testFleetConfig`, so unrelated unit specs do not skip watches. Extend `fleet.config.spec.ts` parsing/rejection tables alongside flowTickMs, including environment restoration. In `fleet-flow-features.integration.spec.ts`, set `FLEET_FLOW_MERGE_POLL_MS=1000` before `bootHttpApp` and restore it after: its existing one-second ticks must still poll. Add the real ticker/advance seam case there with a non-forge getPullRequest error on every call, proving STOPPED/internal_error on tick five. Keep forge I/O outside transactions and treat retry, idle and exceptions distinctly from watched.

**Scope** — In: merge interval config, completed-watch timestamp retention, polling boundary behavior and real ticker error-stop integration. Out: ticker counting/cursor implementation is US-004; stop primitive is US-003.
- A database column or migration for the flow failure counts, the ticker cursor or the merge-watch timestamps; they are in-memory because the API is single-replica by ruling.
- Splitting `fleet-flow-advance.service.ts` (1008 lines) below the 800-line limit; new flow-stop selection logic goes into `fleet-flow-feature-passes.ts` instead of growing the service further.

**Interface** — `flowMergePollMs: number`; `FLEET_FLOW_MERGE_POLL_MS`; `FleetFlowAdvanceService.advance(flowId, now)`; `runMergeWatch` outcome `kind: 'watched' | 'retry' | 'idle'`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] fleetConfig() with FLEET_FLOW_MERGE_POLL_MS unset returns flowMergePollMs: 120000.
AC-2 [unit] fleetConfig() with FLEET_FLOW_MERGE_POLL_MS=60000 returns flowMergePollMs: 60000.
AC-3 [unit] Env validation rejects FLEET_FLOW_MERGE_POLL_MS=999 and FLEET_FLOW_MERGE_POLL_MS=3600001.

AC-4 [unit] Two advance calls for one WAITING_MERGE flow whose merge watch resolves with kind watched for an open awaited PR, the second flowMergePollMs - 1 ms after the first, call getPullRequest on the first call only.

AC-5 [unit] Two advance calls for one WAITING_MERGE flow whose merge watch resolves with kind watched for an open awaited PR, the second exactly flowMergePollMs ms after the first, call getPullRequest on both.
AC-6 [unit] When the first advance for a WAITING_MERGE flow rejects because getPullRequest throws a non-forge Error, a second advance 1 ms later calls getPullRequest again.
AC-7 [unit] advance for WAITING_MERGE flow A and then immediately for WAITING_MERGE flow B calls getPullRequest for both.
AC-9 [unit] When the first advance for a WAITING_MERGE flow ends with merge-watch outcome retry (the PR read fails with provider_unreachable), a second advance 1 ms later calls getPullRequest again.

AC-8 [integration] In fleet-flow-features.integration.spec.ts, driving the real FleetFlowTicker.tick with FLEET_FLOW_MERGE_POLL_MS=1000, ticks 1 s apart, and a WAITING_MERGE flow whose getPullRequest stub throws a non-forge Error on every call, the flow reaches state STOPPED with stopReason internal_error on the 5th tick.

AC-10 [unit, failure handling] Given flowMergePollMs=1000 and a WAITING_MERGE flow whose first advance produces merge-watch outcome idle, when the same flow has an awaited PR on a second advance 1 ms later, getPullRequest is called for that PR rather than the watch being skipped.

routing.reasoning: The implementation mirrors the existing interval config and adds a local timestamp check around the existing watched/retry/idle union; existing merge-watch and ticker fixtures support direct TDD despite several mechanical config/test updates.

modifiedFiles.reason: its ticks are 1 s apart on one app and re-tick a WAITING_MERGE flow expecting a fresh `getPullRequest`; set `FLEET_FLOW_MERGE_POLL_MS=1000` before `bootHttpApp` (and restore it after), so every 1 s tick still polls. It also gains this story's AC-8 case (a WAITING_MERGE flow whose `getPullRequest` throws on every call), reusing the file's fixtures.
`testFleetConfig` returns a full `IFleetConfig`; add `flowMergePollMs: 0` so unit specs that use it never skip a merge watch.
the parsing and rejection tables gain `FLEET_FLOW_MERGE_POLL_MS` rows mirroring the `FLEET_FLOW_TICK_MS` rows.

userStories.title: Resolve a flow's reachable project directly
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace the GET flow endpoint's full project-domain listing with a direct reachable-project lookup while retaining its authorization semantics.

**Motivation** — `FleetFlowsController.get` calls `ProjectsService.findAllForPrincipal` and searches the list for the flow's project, so its cost grows with the caller's project count.

**Approach** — `ProjectsService` gains `findReachableById(principal: KodaPrincipal, projectId: string): Promise<ProjectDomain | null>`: the live project when `readsEveryProject(principal)` or `accessibleProjectIds` for the principal includes it, else `null`. A new `PrismaProjectRepository.findLiveById(id)` and `isAccessible(principal: PrincipalRef, projectId)` back it.
`FleetFlowsController.get(flowId, principal)`: calls `projects.findReachableById(principal, flow.projectId)` instead of scanning `findAllForPrincipal`. `null` gives `404 fleet.flows.notFound` with no permission probe; a reachable project without `fleet.flow.read` gives `403`, as today.
The flow-lookup reach check keeps today's semantics exactly: a project is reachable when it is live and the caller either reads every project or holds an access binding for it, the same rule `findAllForPrincipal` applies, now evaluated for one project id. A global Owner or Admin returns at the `readsEveryProject` check without reading any project list; a caller with a `projectId`-null PROJECT binding still pays the `accessibleProjectIds` read, so the gain is largest for global admins and for callers with few bindings.

Reuse membership.queries.ts's binding-only accessibleProjectIds semantics and the existing principal conversions; do not add a new role-claim or legacy-membership check. The repository lookup must filter soft-deleted projects, even for global admins. Update `fleet-flow-read-stop.spec.ts` existing AC-4 and AC-5 to stub `projects.findReachableById` (project and null respectively) and keep their assertions, including no permission probe in AC-5. Cover the service/repository against Postgres and consume the new service through real GET /api/fleet/flows/:flowId. HTTP error checks must account for the normal Nathapp/i18n envelope rather than inventing a new error format.

**Scope** — In: repository/service direct reach seam, GET consumption and user/agent/admin authorization regressions. Out: approval defaults and routes belong to US-001/US-002; flow stopping and polling belong to US-003–US-005. The create endpoint's separate lookup is not part of this optimization.

**Interface** — `findReachableById(principal: KodaPrincipal, projectId: string): Promise<ProjectDomain | null>`; `PrismaProjectRepository.findLiveById(id)`; `isAccessible(principal: PrincipalRef, projectId)`; `FleetFlowsController.get(flowId, principal)`.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] GET /api/fleet/flows/:flowId by a project member holding fleet.flow.read returns 200 with the flow's project slug.
AC-2 [integration] GET /api/fleet/flows/:flowId by a user with no access binding to the flow's project returns 404 with fleet.flows.notFound.
AC-3 [integration] GET /api/fleet/flows/:flowId for a flow whose project is soft-deleted returns 404 with fleet.flows.notFound.
AC-4 [integration] GET /api/fleet/flows/:flowId by a member holding project.read but not fleet.flow.read returns 403.
AC-5 [unit] FleetFlowsController.get calls projects.findReachableById(principal, flow.projectId) and never calls projects.findAllForPrincipal.
AC-6 [integration] ProjectsService.findReachableById for an agent with a project-scoped binding in project P returns P, and for the same agent and a project Q it has no binding in returns null.
AC-7 [integration] ProjectsService.findReachableById for a global Admin user returns any live project and null for a soft-deleted one.

routing.reasoning: Four existing production files gain thin lookup wrappers using readsEveryProject and accessibleProjectIds rather than a new authorization model; visibility and non-disclosure ordering still require the security override.

modifiedFiles.reason: AC-4 and AC-5 stub `projects.findAllForPrincipal`; they now stub `projects.findReachableById` (AC-4 resolves the project, AC-5 resolves `null`) and keep their assertions, including "no permission probe" in AC-5.

userStories.title: Retry note upserts that lose a concurrent write race
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Recover bounded same-slug note upsert races with new serializable transactions and unchanged final exception shapes.

**Motivation** — Two concurrent writers of the same slug both see no active row; the loser fails with a unique violation on `activeKey` or a serialization failure (`P2034`), which reaches the caller as a 500.

**Approach** — `isSerializationFailure(error: unknown): boolean` (new, `apps/api/src/common/utils/prisma-errors.ts`): `true` for a `PrismaClientKnownRequestError` with code `P2034`.
`PrismaMemoryItemRepository.upsert(item, options)`.
- Target: each attempt runs through `this.tx.run(callback, { isolationLevel: 'Serializable' })`. When an attempt rejects with `isUniqueViolation(error, 'activeKey')` or `isSerializationFailure(error)`, it waits `protected retryDelay(attempt: number): Promise<void>` (which sleeps `memoryUpsertBackoffMs(attempt, Math.random)` ms) and runs again, up to the exported `MEMORY_UPSERT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (`3`) attempts. Inside an outer transaction (`this.tx.isInTransaction()`) it makes one attempt. The error that leaves `upsert` is `PrismaErrorMapper.map(error)` for a `P*` error and the error itself otherwise. The exported pure function `memoryUpsertBackoffMs(attempt: number, random: () => number): number` returns `attempt * Math.round(10 + 40 * random())`.
A note upsert retries in a new transaction with the same jittered backoff as `runWithTicketNumberRetry` (`attempt * round(10 + 40 * random())` ms). Each attempt re-runs the whole transaction callback, including `beforeWrite`, `beforeSupersede` and `onWritten`; their writes belong to the failed transaction and roll back with it.
The retry cannot sit on `PrismaService.withTransaction`: that method maps every `P*` error through `PrismaErrorMapper.map` (`@nathapp/nestjs-prisma` 4.1 `prisma.service.js`), so a P2002 arrives as a `PrismaAppException` `DUPLICATE_ENTRY` and a P2034 as an unidentifiable `DATABASE_ERROR`. The attempts run through the repository's transaction manager, `this.tx.run(callback, { isolationLevel: 'Serializable' })`, which joins the same AsyncLocalStorage `AuditRecorder` reads and passes errors through unmapped; the callback writes through `this.tx.getClient()`. The error that finally leaves `upsert` is mapped with `PrismaErrorMapper.map` when it is a `P*` error, so callers see the same exception shapes as before.

Retrying an already-aborted outer transaction is forbidden: detect the outer transaction before attempts and run once. Other errors propagate on their first attempt; when three eligible conflicts exhaust retries, propagate the final error with the required final mapping and do not delay after the last attempt. Reuse isUniqueViolation for adapter index metadata. Prisma 7 with @prisma/adapter-pg reports SQLSTATE 40001/40P01 as P2034.

In `prisma-memory-item.repository.additional.spec.ts`, upsert cases must control the transaction manager's run and return mockPrismaClient from getClient, retaining no-op, supersede and audit assertions. In `outbox-fanout-extraction.integration.spec.ts`, make the TRANSACTION_MANAGER mock's getClient return mockPrismaClient (the existing mock currently returns undefined). Add `apps/api/test/integration/memory/memory-note-concurrent-upsert.integration.spec.ts` for three identical and two different-description concurrent project-note writers. Use real transactions and the shared DB gate; a retry must rerun hooks inside the transaction rather than outside it.

**Scope** — In: upsert conflict recognition, bounded retry/backoff, transaction client/ALS correctness, final error mapping and same-slug persistence. Out: flow failures belong to US-003–US-005.
- US-007 only: retrying any memory write other than `PrismaMemoryItemRepository.upsert`, and more than 3 concurrent same-slug writers (a 4th racer can exhaust its attempts and receive the error).

**Interface** — `isSerializationFailure(error: unknown): boolean`; exported `MEMORY_UPSERT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (`3`); `protected retryDelay(attempt: number): Promise<void>`; `memoryUpsertBackoffMs(attempt: number, random: () => number): number`; `PrismaMemoryItemRepository.upsert(item, options)`.

userStories.title: Use shim-backed login-only identity for GitHub RUN
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give GitHub RUN a login-only forge identity backed by per-call credential shims instead of a startup token file.

**Motivation** — The API ignores `fresh` for RUN, so a readopted RUN waits the full 120 s token wait and then starts without an identity (D/BUG-9), and a RUN longer than the token's life cannot publish.

**Approach** — `HostExecutor.runIdentityEnv(job, jobDir)` in `apps/runner/src/executor/host-executor.ts`.
- Target: a GitHub RUN whose acquired credentials carry a `binDir` returns `{ NAX_FORGE_IDENTITY: 'login-only', NAX_FORGE_LOGIN: job.assign.gitIdentity.name }`, calls no fresh-token method and writes no file. A GitHub RUN with no `binDir` returns `{}` and logs `RUN starts without a forge identity`. A GitLab RUN returns `{}`. REVIEW and FIX keep `reviewEnv` unchanged. The `binDir` is passed in from the spawn path that already acquires credentials.
`CREDENTIAL_ENV_VARS` in `apps/runner/src/credentials/credential-env.ts` also lists `NAX_FORGE_IDENTITY`.
The RUN identity is login-only only when the job's credential shim directory is on nax's `PATH`. Without the shim, nax's `gh` would use the operator's own `gh` login, so the RUN starts with no injected identity.
`apps/runner/src/credentials/shim.ts` `tokenEnv('gh', reply)`: the `gh` shim sets `GH_TOKEN` from the job's credential-socket reply.
nax `packages/nax/src/forge/identity.ts` `captureForgeIdentity`: `NAX_FORGE_IDENTITY=login-only` requires `NAX_FORGE_LOGIN` and refuses `NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE`.

Pass the binDir already used to build the spawned PATH into the RUN helper; adapt its private parameters as necessary rather than performing another acquire or freshToken call. Overlay the identity after withoutCredentialVars strips inherited identity/token values. Keep token files, fresh waits and cleanup intact for REVIEW and both FIX steps, but RUN must not create forge-token even when spawn fails.

Update the existing Injection harness in `test/unit/host-executor.spec.ts` to return an optional Injection.binDir. Replace #395's fresh-token-file RUN test with login-only/login/no-token-file/no-freshToken assertions; replace refused-fresh-token with the no-binDir warning-and-start case. Replace failed-start cleanup with error propagation and no token file. Remove the obsolete RUN cancelled-token-wait and token-file-write-failure cases. Replace no-fresh-token-provider with a binDir-present case that gets login-only identity and no warning. Replace RUN leftover-token cleanup expectations with no file to remove. In the inherited NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE AC-9, the github row now expects no token file env at all; preserve the gitlab row. Add NAX_FORGE_IDENTITY to credential-env.spec.ts's stripped-variable list.

**Scope** — In: RUN-only identity transport, existing spawn/binDir connection, inherited env sanitization and executor regressions. Out: release secret handling belongs to US-009.

- Making the API honour `fresh` for RUN token requests in `sync.service.ts`; the login-only RUN no longer asks for a fresh token.

**Interface** — RUN overlay `{ NAX_FORGE_IDENTITY: 'login-only', NAX_FORGE_LOGIN: job.assign.gitIdentity.name }` or `{}`; `HostExecutor.runIdentityEnv(job, jobDir)` is the existing private seam, extended to consume acquired binDir; `withoutCredentialVars(env)` strips `NAX_FORGE_IDENTITY`.

AC-2 [unit] Spawning that GitHub RUN passes no NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE and never calls credentials.freshToken.
AC-3 [unit] Spawning that GitHub RUN leaves no forge-token file in the job directory.
AC-4 [unit] Spawning a GitHub RUN whose credentials acquire returns no binDir passes nax neither NAX_FORGE_IDENTITY nor NAX_FORGE_LOGIN, starts nax, and logs RUN starts without a forge identity.
